attributes.description: The example machine that ships with the software: a small production machine with a drive unit behind guarding, an interlocked access door and an emergency stop, assessed under the Machinery Regulation. Every entity type and relationship the metamodel offers is used, and every field holds something, so the example shows what goes where and serves as a fixture for testing. The content is illustrative and carries no engineering judgement about any real machine.
attributes.author: Claude Code
attributes.changes: Every attribute filled and every relationship type used. The Regulation's clauses taken from the catalogue with their headings. Elimination reserved for the one inherently safe design measure, the extra-low voltage controls. The scenarios rated by the risk matrix.
attributes.notes: Reload the example from the File menu at any time to see it as shipped.

attributes.title: Machinery Regulation
attributes.rationale:
The machine is machinery placed on the Union market, so the Regulation applies in full. It replaces Directive 2006/42/EC from 20 January 2027; machinery placed on the market before that date follows the Directive, and this project assumes placement after it.
No exclusion of Annex I applies to this machine.
attributes.notes: The consolidated text is the one on EUR-Lex under the link. Corrigenda are checked at each revision of this project.

attributes.title: Emergency stop
attributes.requirement:
The machinery or related product shall be fitted with one or more emergency stop devices to enable actual or impending danger to be averted.

The following exceptions apply:

(a) the machinery or related product in which an emergency stop device would not lessen the risk, either because it would not reduce the stopping time or because it would not enable the special measures required to deal with the risk to be taken;

(b) portable hand-held or hand-guided machinery or related products.

The device shall:

(a) have clearly identifiable, clearly visible and quickly accessible control devices;

(b) stop the hazardous process as quickly as possible, without creating additional risks;

(c) where necessary, trigger or permit the triggering of certain safeguard movements.

Once active operation of the emergency stop device has ceased following a stop command, that command shall be sustained by engagement of the emergency stop device until that engagement is specifically overridden; it shall not be possible to engage the device without triggering a stop command; it shall be possible to disengage the device only by an appropriate operation, and disengaging the device shall not restart the machinery or related product but only permit restarting.

The emergency stop function shall be available and operational at all times, regardless of the operating mode.

Emergency stop devices shall be a backup to other safeguarding measures and not a substitute for them.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide treats the emergency stop as a complementary measure that never replaces safeguarding, and asks that every operating position occupied while the machine can move has one within reach.
attributes.rationale:
The machine has an operating position occupied while the drives can move, and none of the exemptions applies: it is neither portable hand-held nor hand-guided machinery, and stopping is not made more hazardous by an emergency stop.
A mushroom-head device is fitted at the operating position and realised by the Emergency Stop safety function.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Protection against mechanical risks
attributes.notes: A heading of Annex III, kept so the clauses beneath it stand as the Regulation files them. It is not assessed.

attributes.title: Risks related to moving parts
attributes.requirement:
The moving parts of the machinery or related product shall be designed and constructed in such a way as to prevent risks of contact which could lead to accidents or shall, where risks persist, be fitted with guards or protective devices.

All necessary steps shall be taken to prevent accidental blockage of moving parts. In cases where, despite the precautions taken, a blockage is likely to occur, the necessary specific protective devices and tools shall, when appropriate, be provided to enable the equipment to be safely unblocked.

The instructions for use and, where possible, a sign on the machinery or related product shall identify these specific protective devices and how they are to be used.

The prevention of risks of contact leading to hazardous situations and the psychological stress that may be caused by the interaction with the machinery shall be adapted to:

(a) human-machine coexistence in a shared space without direct collaboration;

(b) human-machine interaction.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide reads this requirement together with the guard requirements. Where contact cannot be prevented by design, the choice between a fixed guard and an interlocked one follows how often access is needed.
attributes.rationale: The drive unit carries rotating and translating parts in the product path, and the path must stay reachable for jam clearing, so contact cannot be prevented by design alone. The residual risk is taken by guarding, which is why 1.4.2 applies below.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Required characteristics of guards and protective devices
attributes.notes: A heading of Annex III, kept so the clauses beneath it stand as the Regulation files them. It is not assessed.

attributes.title: Special requirements for guards
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide expects fixed guards to need a tool to remove and interlocked guards to stop the hazardous function before access is possible.
attributes.rationale: Guarding is the measure chosen for 1.3.7, so the guard requirements bind. The fixed panels are assessed under 1.4.2.1 and the access door under 1.4.2.2.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Fixed guards
attributes.requirement:
Fixed guards shall be fixed by systems that can be opened or removed only with tools.

Their fixing systems shall remain attached to the guards or to the machinery or related product when the guards are removed.

Where possible, guards shall be incapable of remaining in place without their fixings.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide reads the fastening requirement as captive fasteners, so a guard cannot be put back with fasteners missing.
attributes.rationale: The panels enclosing the drive area are fixed guards. Their fasteners stay attached to the guard when it is removed, and a tool is needed to remove them.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Interlocking movable guards
attributes.requirement:
Interlocking movable guards shall:

(a) as far as possible remain attached to the machinery or related product when open;

(b) be designed and constructed in such a way that they can be adjusted only by means of an intentional action.

Interlocking movable guards shall be associated with an interlocking device that:

(a) prevents the start of hazardous machinery or related product functions until those guards are closed; and

(b) gives a stop command whenever those guards are no longer closed.

Where it is possible for an operator to reach the danger zone before the risk due to the hazardous machinery or related product functions has ceased, movable guards shall be associated with a guard locking device in addition to an interlocking device that:

(a) prevents the start of hazardous machinery or related product functions until the guard is closed and locked; and

(b) keeps the guard closed and locked until the risk of injury from the hazardous machinery or related product functions has ceased.

Interlocking movable guards shall be designed in such a way that the absence or failure of one of their components prevents starting or stops the hazardous machinery or related product functions.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide asks for guard locking wherever the hazardous function does not stop before access is possible.
attributes.rationale: The access door is an interlocking movable guard with guard locking, since the drive runs on after a stop command. It is realised by the Door Interlock safety function.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Risks due to other causes
attributes.notes: A heading of Annex III, kept so the clauses beneath it stand as the Regulation files them. It is not assessed.

attributes.title: Electrical supply
attributes.requirement:
Where machinery or related products have an electricity supply, they shall be designed, constructed and equipped in such a way that all hazards of an electrical nature are or can be prevented.

The safety objectives set out in Directive 2014/35/EU shall apply to machinery or related products. However, the obligations concerning conformity assessment and the placing on the market or putting into service of machinery or related products with regard to electrical risks are governed solely by this Regulation.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide points to the electrical equipment standard as the usual way of meeting this requirement.
attributes.rationale: The machine is supplied with mains electricity and its cabinet holds terminals that stay live when the main switch is off, so the electrical hazards are present and this requirement is assessed in full.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Extreme temperatures
attributes.requirement:
Steps shall be taken to eliminate any risk of injury arising from contact with or proximity to machinery or related product parts or materials at high or very low temperatures.

The necessary steps shall also be taken to avoid or protect against the risk of hot or very cold material being ejected.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide reads this as covering surfaces a person can touch in intended use and foreseeable misuse, cleaning included.
attributes.rationale: The surfaces of the drive stay hot after a run and are reached when the machine is cleaned. Contact cannot be prevented by design, so the hazard is marked and the instructions give a cooling time.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Laser radiation
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: Not consulted, since the requirement does not apply.
attributes.rationale:
The machine carries no laser equipment: no laser is used for sensing, marking, alignment or any other function, and none is foreseen for the configurations covered by this assessment. Nothing in the machine can emit laser radiation, so the requirement has no subject here.
If a laser sensor is ever fitted, this verdict is reopened.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Maintenance
attributes.notes: A heading of Annex III, kept so the clauses beneath it stand as the Regulation files them. It is not assessed.

attributes.title: Isolation of energy sources
attributes.requirement:
Machinery or related products shall be fitted with means to isolate it from all energy sources. Such isolators shall be clearly identified. They shall be capable of being locked if reconnection could endanger persons. Isolators shall also be capable of being locked where an operator is unable, from any of the points to which he or she has access, to check that the energy is still cut off.

In the case of machinery or related products capable of being plugged into an electricity supply, removal of the plug is sufficient, if the operator can check from any of the points to which he or she has access that the plug remains removed.

After the energy is cut off, it shall be possible to dissipate normally any energy remaining or stored in the circuits of the machinery or related product without risk to persons.

As an exception to the requirement laid down in the previous paragraphs, certain circuits may remain connected to their energy sources in order, for example, to hold parts, to protect information, to light interiors, etc. In this case, special steps shall be taken to ensure operator safety.
attributes.guidanceSource: Guide to application of the Machinery Regulation
attributes.guidance: The guide asks for the isolating device to be lockable where reconnection could endanger, and for stored energy to be dissipated or retained safely.
attributes.rationale: Maintenance and cleaning are carried out inside the guarding, where reconnection would endanger the person working there, so a lockable isolating device is required. The drive also stores energy after the supply is removed, which the isolation procedure has to account for.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it, taken from the catalogue. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: EMC Directive
attributes.rationale:
The machine carries electrical equipment that can generate and is susceptible to electromagnetic disturbance, so the Directive applies alongside the Machinery Regulation.
The fixed installation exclusion does not apply: the machine is placed on the market as a finished product.
Open: whether the drive supplier’s declaration covers the installed configuration, or only the drive as a component.
attributes.notes: The drive supplier is asked for the declaration covering the installed configuration.

attributes.title: General requirements — emission
attributes.requirement: Equipment shall be designed and manufactured, having regard to the state of the art, so that the electromagnetic disturbance it generates does not exceed the level above which radio and telecommunications equipment or other equipment cannot operate as intended.
attributes.rationale: The machine carries variable-speed drives and switching control gear, which are sources of conducted and radiated disturbance, so the emission requirement applies to the machine as placed on the market.
attributes.guidance: The guide asks the manufacturer to consider the emission of the assembled machine, not only of its components.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: General requirements — immunity
attributes.requirement: Equipment shall be designed and manufactured, having regard to the state of the art, so that it has a level of immunity to the electromagnetic disturbance to be expected in its intended use which allows it to operate without unacceptable degradation of its intended use.
attributes.rationale:
The safety-related control system has to keep working in the disturbance of an industrial installation, so the verdict turns on what unacceptable degradation means for the safety functions rather than on whether the requirement is met in general.
Left unassessed until the immunity test report is in: the open question is whether a degradation that trips the machine to a safe state counts as acceptable here.
attributes.guidance: The guide leaves what counts as unacceptable degradation to the intended use, which for a safety function is what this project has to decide.
attributes.notes: Text of the requirement as the Official Journal has it. The applicability verdict is this project's own.

attributes.title: Machine
attributes.description: The machinery placed on the market.
attributes.manufacturer: Example Machines, the manufacturer in this example
attributes.characteristics: Floor standing. Three-phase supply. One operating position at the loading side. One access door on the drive side.
attributes.notes: The machinery placed on the market, as one unit.

attributes.title: Control System
attributes.description: Controls the machine, evaluates the safety inputs and carries the operator controls.
attributes.characteristics: A programmable controller for the production programme and a separate safety controller for the safety functions.
attributes.notes: The safety-related part is the safety controller beneath.

attributes.title: Safety Controller
attributes.description: Safety-related part of the control system.
attributes.manufacturer: A safety controller supplier, not named
attributes.characteristics: Two channels with cross monitoring. Safe outputs for the drive enable. Rated by its supplier to the performance level claimed.
attributes.notes: Type-examined as a safety component.

attributes.title: Emergency Stop Device
attributes.description: Mushroom-head device at the operating position.
attributes.manufacturer: A control gear supplier, not named
attributes.characteristics: Red on yellow. Latches when pressed and is released by turning. Two normally closed contacts.
attributes.notes: One device, at the operating position.

attributes.title: Unexpected Start-up
attributes.description: Mechanical hazard. The machine starts while someone is inside the guarding.
attributes.rationale: A start while someone is inside the guarding is prevented by the interlock and the emergency stop, not eliminated.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.title: Operator Controls
attributes.description: The pushbuttons and the display at the operating position, run on 24 volts.
attributes.characteristics: Extra-low voltage throughout. No part at the operating position carries supply voltage.
attributes.notes: The one place the example applies an inherently safe design measure.

attributes.title: Live Parts at the Controls
attributes.description: Electrical hazard. Parts at supply voltage within reach at the operating position, as there would be with controls at mains voltage.
attributes.rationale: Eliminated by design. The controls run on 24 volts, so nothing at the operating position can give a shock, whatever fails. This is what makes the measure inherent rather than protective.
attributes.notes: The protected supply was first related as eliminating this hazard and unrelated when it was seen to be protection, so the record still names it and the hazard carries a message to revisit. It is left so on purpose, to show the messages.

attributes.title: Drive Unit
attributes.description: Motor and gearbox driving the moving parts.
attributes.characteristics: Rotating and translating parts in the product path. Runs on after a stop command until standstill. Surfaces stay hot after a run.
attributes.notes: Every mechanical and thermal hazard of the machine sits here.

attributes.title: Moving Parts
attributes.description: Mechanical hazard. Rotating and translating parts in the drive area.
attributes.rationale: The moving parts are needed for the function of the machine and cannot be designed out, so the hazard is guarded rather than eliminated.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.title: Stored Energy
attributes.description: Mechanical hazard. Energy held in the drive after the supply is removed.
attributes.rationale: The drive stores energy after the supply is removed. It is retained safely and released by the isolation procedure rather than eliminated.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.title: Hot Surface
attributes.description: Thermal hazard. Surfaces of the drive that stay hot after a run.
attributes.rationale: The surfaces heat by the nature of the drive and cannot be kept cool by design, so the hazard is marked and covered by the cleaning procedure.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.title: Guarding
attributes.description: Fixed panels enclosing the drive area, with one access door.
attributes.characteristics: Fixed panels held by captive fasteners. One access door with a coded interlock and guard locking.
attributes.notes: The guards this project assesses the guard requirements against.

attributes.title: Interlock Switch
attributes.description: Coded interlocking device on the guard door.
attributes.model: Coded interlocking device with guard locking
attributes.characteristics: Two channels. Coded actuator. Locking held until standstill is signalled.
attributes.notes: Fixed so that it cannot be removed without a tool.

attributes.title: Electrical Cabinet
attributes.description: Houses the supply, the drives and the control gear.
attributes.characteristics: Houses the supply disconnecting device, the drives and the control gear. Incoming terminals stay live when the main switch is off.
attributes.notes: Opened by the technician only, with the supply isolated.

attributes.title: Live Parts
attributes.description: Electrical hazard. Terminals that stay live when the main switch is off.
attributes.rationale: The incoming terminals stay live by the nature of the supply. Access is controlled by the isolation procedure.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.title: Short Circuit
attributes.description: Electrical hazard. A fault current in the electrical equipment.
attributes.rationale: A fault current cannot be ruled out by design. The supply is protected so that a fault is interrupted, which is protection, since a protective device can fail, and not elimination.
attributes.notes: Recorded from the hazard identification of the example. The measures field is the record the software keeps of what was related as eliminating the hazard when Eliminated was set, and nothing eliminates this one.

attributes.familiarity: Assumed to know this machine daily, and its hazards from the induction.
attributes.notes: The person most often at the machine.

attributes.familiarity: Assumed to know machines of this kind well, and this one from its documentation.

attributes.familiarity: Assumed to know this machine from the induction, not from daily use.

attributes.title: Contact with Moving Parts
attributes.hazardousEvent: Operator reaches into the drive area to clear a jam. Drive starts while the hand is in the hazard zone.
attributes.initialSeverityRationale: A hand caught between moving parts is crushed, an injury that does not heal fully.
attributes.initialProbabilityRationale: Jams are cleared a few times a shift, and reaching in is the quickest way.
attributes.residualSeverityRationale: The harm, if the drive starts with a hand inside, is the same.
attributes.residualProbabilityRationale: The door is locked until standstill, so the drive cannot move while a hand is inside.
attributes.evaluation: The residual risk is acceptable. The interlocked guard with locking removes the occurrence, and the instructions cover the rest.
attributes.notes: Rated by the risk matrix chosen in the project settings. The other methods hold values too, so the project can switch methods and see every field.

attributes.title: Electric Shock
attributes.hazardousEvent: Technician works in the cabinet with the supply connected. Contact with a live part.
attributes.initialSeverityRationale: Contact with a live terminal at supply voltage can kill.
attributes.initialProbabilityRationale: The cabinet is opened monthly, and the terminals are marked.
attributes.residualProbabilityRationale: The isolation procedure and the lock make contact with a live part a deliberate act.
attributes.evaluation: The residual risk is acceptable. Isolation is required before the cabinet is opened, and the incoming terminals are covered and marked.
attributes.notes: Rated by the risk matrix chosen in the project settings. The other methods hold values too, so the project can switch methods and see every field.

attributes.title: Start-up During Maintenance
attributes.hazardousEvent: Technician inside the guarding with the machine not isolated. Machine restarts.
attributes.initialSeverityRationale: A restart with a person inside the guarding crushes.
attributes.initialProbabilityRationale: Maintenance is done inside the guarding monthly, and a restart by another person is foreseeable.
attributes.residualProbabilityRationale: With the supply isolated and locked, a restart is not possible.
attributes.evaluation: The residual risk is acceptable. The lock is personal to the technician, and the emergency stop remains available.
attributes.notes: Rated by the risk matrix chosen in the project settings. The other methods hold values too, so the project can switch methods and see every field.

attributes.title: Burn on Hot Surface
attributes.hazardousEvent: Cleaner works close to the drive after a production run. Contact with a hot surface.
attributes.initialSeverityRationale: A burn to the hand from a hot surface, treatable on site.
attributes.initialProbabilityRationale: Cleaning is done after every run, when the drive is hottest.
attributes.residualProbabilityRationale: The marking and the cooling time in the instructions keep the hand off the surface.
attributes.evaluation: The residual risk is acceptable. A burn is minor and the marking and the instructions make it unlikely.
attributes.notes: Rated by the risk matrix chosen in the project settings. The warning marking was related after the residual risk was rated, so this scenario carries a message to revisit. It is left so on purpose, to show the messages.

attributes.title: Fixed Guard
attributes.description: Panels that enclose the drive area.
attributes.notes: Removable only with a tool, fasteners captive.

attributes.title: Interlocked Guard
attributes.description: Access door with a coded interlock and guard locking.
attributes.notes: Realised by the Door Interlock safety function.

attributes.title: Emergency Stop
attributes.description: Device that stops the machine on demand.
attributes.notes: A complementary measure. It never replaces the guarding.

attributes.title: Energy Isolation
attributes.description: Lockable device that removes the electrical supply.
attributes.notes: The procedure is part of the instructions for use.

attributes.title: Warning Label
attributes.description: Marking at the hot surface of the drive.
attributes.notes: Pictogram for a hot surface, placed at the drive.

attributes.title: Instructions for Use
attributes.description: Procedure for clearing a jam with the machine stopped.
attributes.notes: The procedure for clearing a jam and the cooling time before cleaning.

attributes.title: Extra-low Voltage Controls
attributes.description: The controls at the operating position run on 24 volts, so no live part at supply voltage is within reach there. The hazard is removed, not guarded.
attributes.notes: The one measure of the first step in this example. A guard, a stop, an isolator or a marking reduces a risk, and only a design measure like this one eliminates a hazard.

attributes.title: Protected Supply
attributes.description: Fuses and a residual current device in the cabinet interrupt a fault current before it can harm.
attributes.notes: Protection, not elimination. A protective device can fail, so the hazard it guards against remains.

attributes.title: Emergency Stop
attributes.description: Stops all drives when an emergency stop device is operated.
attributes.trigger: An emergency stop device is operated.
attributes.reaction: Power is removed from all drives, stop category 0.
attributes.safeState: All drives at standstill and restart inhibited.
attributes.feedback: The device latches and stays visibly pressed. The controller reports the stop on the operator display.
attributes.restart: The device is released by turning it, and the machine restarts only by a deliberate start command.
attributes.designTargets: Category 1, one channel with well-tried components.
attributes.interfaces: The device contacts to the safety controller. The safe outputs of the controller to the drive enable.
attributes.independence: Independent of the production programme. Shares the safety controller with the door interlock.
attributes.defeating: The device is not muted in any mode and cannot be bypassed without opening the cabinet.
attributes.environment: Indoor, industrial, at the temperatures and humidity the cabinet is rated for.
attributes.faultsDetected: A stuck contact of the device. A welded output of the controller.
attributes.detectionMeans: The device contacts are monitored for plausibility at each operation. The outputs are read back at each cycle.
attributes.faultHandling: The drive enable is removed and the machine stays stopped until the fault is cleared.
attributes.faultIndication: A fault message on the operator display and a fault output to the controller.
attributes.faultRecovery: A fault latches until it is cleared by a technician and the function is tested.
attributes.powerDisturbances: Loss of supply removes the drive enable, which is the safe state. Return of supply does not restart the machine.
attributes.notes: A complementary measure. The Door Interlock is the safeguarding.

attributes.title: Door Interlock
attributes.description: Stops the drives when the guard door is opened and keeps the door locked until standstill.
attributes.trigger: The guard door leaves the closed position.
attributes.reaction: Power is removed from the drives, stop category 0, and the door lock is released once standstill is reached.
attributes.safeState: Drives at standstill, restart inhibited, door free to open.
attributes.feedback: The lock is visibly released. The controller reports the door as open.
attributes.muting: Never muted or overridden. There is no mode that runs the machine with the door open.
attributes.restart: The door is closed and locked, then a deliberate start command restarts the machine.
attributes.designTargets: Category 3, two channels with cross monitoring.
attributes.interfaces: The position detection to the safety controller. The safe outputs of the controller to the drive enable and to the lock.
attributes.independence: Independent of the production programme. Shares the safety controller with the emergency stop.
attributes.defeating: A coded actuator that cannot be replaced by a spare, and a device fixed so that it cannot be removed without a tool.
attributes.faultsDetected: A discrepancy between the two channels of the position detection. A welded output. A lock that fails to hold.
attributes.detectionMeans: Cross monitoring of the two channels at each cycle. Read-back of the outputs. The lock monitored by its own contact.
attributes.faultHandling: The drive enable is removed and the machine stays stopped until the fault is cleared.
attributes.faultIndication: A fault message on the operator display and a fault output to the controller.
attributes.faultRecovery: A fault latches until it is cleared by a technician and the function is tested.
attributes.powerDisturbances: Loss of supply removes the drive enable and holds the lock, which is the safe state. Return of supply does not restart the machine.
attributes.notes: The safeguarding for the drive area. Decomposed into the position detection and the safe torque off.

attributes.title: Position Detection
attributes.description: Detects the guard door position on two channels.
attributes.trigger: The guard door leaves the closed position.
attributes.reaction: Both channels signal open to the safety controller.
attributes.feedback: None of its own. The parent function reports.
attributes.interfaces: The two channels of the interlocking device to the safety controller.
attributes.defeating: Coded actuator. Device fixed with a tool.
attributes.environment: Indoor, industrial. The device rated for the door's cycles.
attributes.faultsDetected: A discrepancy between the channels. A stuck actuator.
attributes.faultHandling: The parent function removes the drive enable.
attributes.powerDisturbances: Loss of supply reads as open, which is the safe direction.
attributes.notes: A subfunction of the Door Interlock.

attributes.title: Safe Torque Off
attributes.description: Removes torque from the drives on two channels.
attributes.trigger: A stop is demanded by the safety controller.
attributes.reaction: The drive enable is removed on both channels.
attributes.feedback: The drive reports the safe torque off state to the controller.
attributes.restart: The enable is restored only with a deliberate start command.
attributes.designTargets: Category 3, two channels, read-back from the drive.
attributes.interfaces: The safe outputs of the safety controller to the drive's safe torque off inputs.
attributes.independence: Independent of the drive's own control.
attributes.defeating: The inputs are inside the cabinet, opened only with the supply isolated.
attributes.faultsDetected: A welded output. A drive that does not report the state.
attributes.detectionMeans: Read-back of the drive's state at each cycle.
attributes.faultHandling: The parent function keeps the machine stopped.
attributes.powerDisturbances: Loss of supply removes the torque, which is the safe state.
attributes.notes: A subfunction of the Door Interlock.

attributes.title: Access Protection
attributes.description: The machine shall prevent access to the drive area while the drives can move.
attributes.rationale: Access to the drive area is the common cause of the recorded scenarios.
attributes.notes: The parent of the guarding requirements.

attributes.title: Guard Fastening
attributes.description: The machine shall retain fixed guards with fasteners that stay attached to the guard.
attributes.rationale: Loose fasteners are why a guard is left off after maintenance.
attributes.notes: Expresses the fixed guard.

attributes.title: Guard Interlocking
attributes.description: While the drives can move, the machine shall keep the guard door locked closed.
attributes.rationale: The drives overrun after a stop command.
attributes.notes: Expresses the door interlock.

attributes.title: Emergency Stop Devices
attributes.description: The machine shall provide an emergency stop device at each operating position.
attributes.rationale: Required at every position occupied while the machine can move.
attributes.notes: Derived from the essential requirement on the emergency stop.

attributes.title: Supply Isolation
attributes.description: The machine shall provide a lockable device that isolates the electrical supply.
attributes.rationale: Maintenance is carried out inside the guarding.
attributes.notes: Expresses the energy isolation.

attributes.title: Emergency Stop Test
attributes.description: Operate each emergency stop device during a cycle. Release it and attempt a restart without a start command.
attributes.setup: The machine running the production programme with no material loaded.
attributes.acceptanceCriteria: All drives stop and the machine does not restart on release.
attributes.runs: 2026-09-20	Commissioning engineer	Passed	Both stops within the response time. No restart on release.
attributes.notes: Repeated at each commissioning.

attributes.title: Interlock Test
attributes.description: Open the guard door during a cycle. Time the release of the lock against standstill.
attributes.setup: The machine running the production programme with no material loaded. A stopwatch at the door.
attributes.acceptanceCriteria: The door stays locked until standstill is reached.
attributes.runs: 2026-09-20	Commissioning engineer	Passed	Lock released after standstill on every attempt.
attributes.notes: Repeated at each commissioning.

attributes.title: Guard Inspection
attributes.description: Remove each fixed guard panel and handle it as maintenance would.
attributes.setup: The machine isolated and locked. Each fixed guard panel removed in turn.
attributes.acceptanceCriteria: No fastener separates from the guard without a tool.
attributes.runs: 2026-09-19	Maintenance technician	Passed	All fasteners captive.
attributes.notes: Repeated when a guard is replaced.

attributes.title: Circuit Analysis
attributes.description: Review the safety circuit against the claimed architecture and reliability data.
attributes.responsible: The functional safety engineer, Example Machines
attributes.setup: The circuit diagrams, the supplier data for the safety controller, the interlock and the drive.
attributes.acceptanceCriteria: The achieved performance level is not lower than the required one for each safety function.
attributes.runs: 2026-09-15	Functional safety engineer	Passed	PL d achieved for the door interlock, PL c for the emergency stop.
attributes.notes: Redone when a safety-related part is replaced by another type.
